Definition: Shenir or Senir, a summit of Lebanon
BiblicalUsage: Shenir is the name the Amorites give Mount Hermon, and the Sidonians call the same peak Sirion. The men of the east hold it, the Song counts it among the peaks, and the ships of Tyre are built from its fir trees.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a mountain with three names is a mountain everyone wanted, and Hermon is the high place that watches over the land. I hold that the peaks of the Bible are God's watchtowers, and Shenir is one of them.
